title: Apex SDK mini-sprint quickboard (telemetry-first)
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, 1-day "mini-sprint" sketch to produce a single-page, telemetry-first SDK quickstart and a tiny sandbox lab app that engineers can complete in ~60 minutes. Goal is a reproducible, instrumented onboarding path that surfaces the signals we care about (latency, token cost, error classes, KV-cache hit rate) and includes a minimal failure-injection step so integrators understand graceful degradation.

Audience:
- Backend engineers integrating Redwood SDKs into a service
- Solutions engineers running customer demos
- Developer advocates who need a deterministic demo flow

High-level deliverables (end of mini-sprint):
- one-pager quickstart (copy + minimal sample app) emphasising three telemetry checks
- instrumented sample app (node/python) with 6 smoke tests and a failure-injection toggle
- checklist for first-10-mins diagnostics and SLO gating
- short slide (3) for internal handoff to support/sales with expected signals and escalation paths

Proposed agenda (single day):
- 09:00 - 09:20: Kickoff, scope & acceptance criteria
- 09:20 - 10:30: Draft quickstart copy + minimal cli commands (pair)
- 10:30 - 12:00: Implement sample app: request path, telemetry hooks, simple UI or CLI toggle
- 12:00 - 13:00: Lunch + smoke test plan writeup
- 13:00 - 14:30: Add failure injection & KV-cache demo scenarios
- 14:30 - 15:30: Create 6 smoke tests (latency, 4xx, 5xx, token usage, cache hit, fallback route)
- 15:30 - 16:15: Internal demo & iterate on copy/observability snapshots
- 16:15 - 17:00: Write handoff notes, Confluence stub, open PR for sample app

Quickstart one-page (structure notes):
- TL;DR in one command (curl + example response)
- install + auth (env var pattern, local stub option)
- 3 example flows: generate, chat, embeddings (single-line calls)
- telemetry checklist (what to look at in Console within first 10 minutes)
- fallback advice + minimal retry policy
- where to file a ticket / expected artifact to attach

Telemetry checklist (minimal required signals):
- median P95 latency for small payload (<= 200 tokens) — expected baseline: 40-120ms host; note: vary by model
- per-call token cost vs total session tokens — show simple command to capture tokens in sample app
- error breakdown: 4xx (client), 429 (rate), 5xx (infrastructure) — map each to suggested next step
- KV cache hit rate for conversational flows (toggle show/hide)
- fallback incidence: count of requests that hit fallback path (model-variant fallback)

Sample app sketch (what it must include):
- two endpoints: /generate and /chat-session
- a small in-memory KV cache with a TTL and a "force-miss" query param for demoing cache-miss behavior
- telemetry hooks that emit structured logs: {request_id, model, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, cache_hit, error_class}
- lightweight local mode: REDWOOD_LOCAL=true to run against a stubbed server (for offline demos)
- a toggle to flip to a cheaper quantized model to exercise fallback path and show cost delta

Smoke tests (6 minimal):
1) simple generate returns 200 and token count > 0
2) chat-session retains KV cache across two messages (cache_hit true on second)
3) large payload (2k tokens) returns within SLO (note SLO varies by model)
4) injected 5xx from server -> sample app retries once then surfaces graceful message to client
5) fallback to quantized model triggers and lowers token cost on subsequent calls
6) metrics emitted to console/console-mock with expected fields present

Failure injection plan (very small):
- add header X-FI: 5xx or X-FI: slow(500ms) to simulate infra disturbance
- sample app should expose a debug route /fi that sets mode for next 5 requests
- provide scripts in repo to flip failure mode and run smoke tests automatically

Acceptance criteria (for mini-sprint):
- one-pager quickstart in repo root and in Drive Confluence stub
- sample app runs locally with REDWOOD_LOCAL=true and demo script completes
- telemetry artifacts in logs match the checklist fields for 80% of runs
- PR opened for sample app + quickstart copy with reviewers assigned: eng-developer-experience, eng-serving-runtime, solutions-eng

Open questions / notes to self: (keep short)
- which model variant names should we use in examples to avoid frequent churn? maybe use model tags instead of exact names
- do we include SDK install for both npm/pip or only npm first? suggest provide both but prioritize one in live demo
- small UX friction: env var naming conventions across repos — unify to REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_LOCAL
- supportability: need a short escalation doc for SRE showing logs to attach (traces + sample request id)

Handoff checklist for support/sales (3 bullets):
- exact commands to reproduce demo + expected telemetry screenshots
- list of common troubleshooting steps (env var, region mismatch, model name mismatch, token budget exceeded)
- pointer to JIRA template for escalations and required attachments (request_id, console screenshot, smoke test output)

Next todos (post-mini-sprint):
- (Maya) Draft quickstart one-pager and open PR — due in 48h
- (Liam) Implement failure-injection helper and smoke test harness — due in 72h
- (Priya) Add telemetry example dashboards + JSON snippets for console export — due in 96h
- (Evelyn) Draft 3-slide handoff deck for sales/support — due in 5 days

Contact / follow-up:
- Slack: #devexp (pin the PR once opened)
- Demo window proposal: next Tue 10:00 for internal review

Raw snippets / copy ideas (quick grab):
- "Try it in 60s: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=... && node tiny-demo.js && curl localhost:3000/generate -d '{"prompt":"Hello"}'"
- "Telemetry tip: filter logs by request_id and look for cache_hit === true to confirm conversational state reuse"

Unresolved: do we want to include a short video (30s) for the handoff slide? likely yes but out of scope for this mini-sprint.

End of sketch.
